cause_quote: The new migrations.memory.apply handler called `runMigrationApply({ runtime: silentRuntime, ..., opts: { yes: true, json: true, ... allowPartialResult: true } })` with no backupOutput, so the pre-migration backup fell to the backup engine's current-directory default.
user_saw: A memory import from the Control UI or onboarding wrote the pre-migration backup archive into whatever folder the Gateway or onboarding process was started from, such as a source checkout.
summary: Adds a preferHomeOutput backup option so Gateway memory imports and onboarding migrations write their unattended pre-migration backup to the home folder instead of the process cwd.
reasoning: The local history is grafted at b14a2cae (2026-09-03), so I traced the Gateway memory import through gh api to its introduction in #106406, whose runMigrationApply call passes no backup output and therefore always used the cwd default that the fix overrides; onboarding (#108977) reused the same path. Nothing later changed the cwd default, so the misplaced archive shipped with the feature; confidence is medium because the pre-graft backup default was not re-read line by line.
